# SparseApplyAdagrad

<!-- codespell:ignore accum adagrad -->

| <term>Atlas A2 products</term>                               |    √     |

## Function

- Operator function: SparseApplyAdagrad is the sparse update operator of the Adagrad optimization algorithm. It selects the corresponding rows in `var` and `accum` according to `indices`, and updates the parameter variable and the gradient square accumulator in place with the sparse gradient `grad`. Rows not hit by `indices` remain unchanged. This operator is commonly used in large-scale sparse parameter training scenarios such as Embedding.

- Formula:

For each index `index = indices[i]` in `indices`:

$$
\text{accum}_{\text{new}}[\text{index}] =
\begin{cases}
\text{accum}_{\text{old}}[\text{index}] + \text{grad}[i]^2, & \text{update\_slots} = \text{True} \\
\text{accum}_{\text{old}}[\text{index}], & \text{update\_slots} = \text{False}
\end{cases}
$$

$$
\text{var}_{\text{new}}[\text{index}] =
\text{var}_{\text{old}}[\text{index}] - \text{lr} \times
\frac{\text{grad}[i]}{\sqrt{\text{accum}_{\text{new}}[\text{index}]} + 10^{-8}}
$$

Here, `1e-8` is a fixed float32 numerical stability constant inside the kernel.

## Constraints

- var and accum must have the same shape, and the rank is at least 2.
- lr must be a scalar, with shape [] or [1].
- indices must be a 1D vector.
- The rank of grad must be the same as that of var. grad.shape[0] must equal indices.shape[0], and grad.shape[1:] must equal var.shape[1:].
- The data types of var, accum, lr, and grad must be consistent. Currently, only float32 is supported.
- The data type of indices currently supports only int32.
- The values in indices must satisfy 0 <= indices[i] < var.shape[0] and should be unique. If indices contains duplicate values, the result is unpredictable.
- epsilon is fixed to float32 1e-8 and is not an input parameter.
- use_locking is integrated as a compatibility attribute. Currently, no additional concurrency semantics are guaranteed.
